vopros: Should I pay for a tool that tracks whether ChatGPT and other AI assistants mention my business, or hire someone to get my business recommended by AI?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Potentially, but I’d separate “measurement” from “optimization.” For most small and midsize businesses, I would not start by paying an agency to “get you recommended by AI.” I’d first determine whether AI recommendations are actually an important acquisition channel for your customers.

AI visibility is becoming measurable. OpenAI says public sites can appear in ChatGPT Search and recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot; ChatGPT referral traffic can also be identified in analytics. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856?utm_source=openai)) Microsoft added AI Performance to Bing Webmaster Tools in 2026, showing citations and pages referenced across its AI experiences. Google has likewise introduced reporting for its generative-AI search features. ([blogs.bing.com](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/February-2026/Introducing-AI-Performance-in-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-Public-Preview?utm_source=openai)) So before buying another dashboard, check the free/first-party data available to you.

The bigger caution is the “AI optimization” sales pitch. There isn't a reliable switch someone can flip to make ChatGPT recommend a company. Google explicitly says its traditional SEO fundamentals remain foundational for its generative-AI features and that no special AI markup is required. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features?utm_source=openai)) OpenAI similarly describes discoverability requirements rather than a paid ranking mechanism. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856?utm_source=openai))

What can be improved is the information ecosystem the assistants draw from: a crawlable and technically sound website, clear pages explaining what you do and who you're for, accurate business/product data, reviews and reputation, authoritative third-party mentions, and content that provides genuinely useful information. For local businesses, things like business listings and consistent location information matter as well. Bing specifically recommends accurate local-business information, while Google emphasizes helpful original content and accurate Business Profile information. ([blogs.bing.com](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/February-2026/Introducing-AI-Performance-in-Bing-Webmaster-Tools-Public-Preview?utm_source=openai))

So I’d spend money in roughly this order:

- First, test 20–50 realistic prompts a prospective customer might ask ChatGPT, Google, Copilot, etc.: “best X in Los Angeles,” “X for someone who needs Y,” comparisons, alternatives, and problem-oriented queries.
- Check your analytics and the free platform tools to see whether AI is already sending traffic/leads.
- If tracking this manually becomes annoying or strategically important, buy a monitoring tool. Treat its “visibility score” as directional, though—AI answers vary by query, context, model, and time.
- Hire someone only if they're going to fix identifiable causes of poor visibility: technical SEO/crawlability, entity/business information, useful content, PR/earned mentions, product feeds, reviews, or conventional SEO.
- Be skeptical of anyone promising “#1 in ChatGPT,” guaranteed recommendations, hundreds of AI-optimized articles, secret GEO/AEO tricks, or special schema that supposedly makes LLMs favor you.

There is one important exception: if you're in a category where customers routinely ask AI to choose providers or products—software, professional services, travel, ecommerce, restaurants, home services, etc.—I'd take this channel more seriously now. For ecommerce specifically, OpenAI supports merchant/product information and direct product feeds, making the work more concrete than generic “GEO.” ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-improved-shopping-results-from-chatgpt-search%25252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525252525253F.mkv?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me what kind of business you have, its approximate revenue/customer value, and whether it's local, ecommerce, B2B, etc., I can tell you whether I'd spend $0, buy a monitoring tool, or hire somebody—and what I'd expect them to actually do.
